episodes.description: In 1959, nine experienced hikers perished in the Ural Mountains under bizarre, inexplicable circumstances that left their tent slashed from the inside. Decades later, investigators remain divided between theories of freak weather phenomena and forces that defy logical explanation.
episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Mystery of Dyatlov Pass
The Wow! Signal: The Mystery of the Mary Celeste
episodes.description: Discovered adrift in the Atlantic Ocean in 1872, the Mary Celeste was found completely abandoned with its cargo intact and personal belongings left behind. To this day, the total disappearance of its crew remains one of the most haunting and enduring maritime puzzles in naval history.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: D.B. Cooper — The Man Who Vanished Mid-Air
episodes.description: In 1971, a man hijacked Flight 305, took $200,000, and parachuted into the night — never to be seen again. The FBI's only unsolved air piracy case.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Somerton Man — The Code No One Could Crack
episodes.description: In 1948, a man was found dead on an Australian beach with no ID — and a scrap of paper in his pocket that read 'Tamám Shud.' It is finished. The code in the book was never cracked.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Zodiac Killer — The Cipher That Took 51 Years to Crack
episodes.description: Between 1968 and 1969, a killer terrorized the San Francisco Bay Area — then mailed his crimes to the newspapers in code. One cipher took 51 years to crack. It named no one.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Bermuda Triangle — Where Ships and Planes Vanish
episodes.description: Draw a triangle between Miami, Bermuda, and Puerto Rico — and you enter the most dangerous water on Earth. Five bombers, a Navy ship, and a tanker vanished there. But the Coast Guard says it is no more dangerous than any other ocean.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Loch Ness Monster — The Photo That Fooled the World
episodes.description: For ninety years, people have sworn a monster lives in Loch Ness. The most famous photo of it was a toy submarine — but the sightings never stopped.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Voynich Manuscript — The Book No One Can Read
episodes.description: Six hundred years old, written in a language no one can read. The world's best codebreakers tried — and failed. The Voynich Manuscript still won't talk.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Night Stalker — The Summer Los Angeles Locked Its Doors
episodes.description: In the summer of 1985, Los Angeles was afraid to sleep. A man the newspapers called the Night Stalker broke into homes at random — until one fingerprint, and the people of East LA, ended it.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Lost Colony of Roanoke — 115 People Vanished Without a Trace
episodes.description: In 1587, 115 English colonists landed on Roanoke Island. Three years later, their governor came back — and they were all gone. One carved word was the only clue.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Flannan Isles — Three Keepers Vanished Without a Trace
episodes.description: In December 1900, three keepers vanished from the Flannan Isles lighthouse. The log stopped, the light went dark — and no one ever saw them again.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: MH370 — 239 People Vanished From the Sky
episodes.description: On March 8, 2014, Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 took off with 239 people aboard — and never landed anywhere. The plane kept flying for seven more hours. The main wreckage has never been found.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Franklin Expedition — 129 Men Vanished in the Arctic
episodes.description: In 1845, HMS Erebus and HMS Terror sailed into the Arctic with 129 men to find the Northwest Passage. None of them came home. The ships were found in 2014 and 2016 — the men never were.

In 525 BC, Cambyses II sent 50,000 men into the Egyptian desert to destroy the Oracle of Amun at Siwa. They reached the Kharga Oasis — and were never seen again. Herodotus says a sandstorm buried them. Scholars are not so sure.
episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Lost Army of Cambyses — 50,000 Men Swallowed by the Desert
The Wow! Signal: The Lost Ninth Legion — 5,000 Soldiers Vanished Without a Trace
episodes.description: In AD 108, Rome's Ninth Legion left one last trace at York — a stone inscription recording the rebuilding of the fortress gate. After that, nothing. No battle report. No survivors. No graves. Mommsen said northern tribes wiped them out in Scotland. But tiles stamped with their mark turned up in Nijmegen, on the Rhine.

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Vanished Anasazi — 30,000 People Walked Away and Never Came Back
episodes.description: By 1300, the Ancestral Puebloans had left the Four Corners — 30,000 people walked away from their cliff cities at Mesa Verde and the great houses of Chaco Canyon. Tree rings say a 23-year drought, 1276 to 1299. But their descendants still live today at Hopi and Zuni — so why did everyone leave at once, and never come back?

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: Amelia Earhart — The Voice That Stopped Over the Pacific
episodes.description: In 1937, Amelia Earhart set out to fly around the world — the first woman ever to try. With navigator Fred Noonan, she had already flown 22,000 miles when she left Lae, New Guinea, for Howland Island on July 2nd. Her last words: 'gas is running low.' The official answer is the plane ran out of fuel and crashed into the Pacific — but some say she landed on a desert island called Nikumaroro and lived there as a castaway. Which side are you on?

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Lost City of Z — Three Men Walked Into the Jungle and Never Came Back
episodes.description: In 1925, British explorer Percy Fawcett walked into the Amazon to find a lost city he called Z — with his son Jack and a friend. On May 29th, they sent their last message — and vanished. A hundred people died looking for them. No bodies. No camp. Nothing. Modern archaeologists have since found great ancient cities in the Amazon — Fawcett was right that something was out there. Which side are you on?

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: MV Joyita — The Empty Ship That Sailed Home
episodes.description: In 1955, the Joyita left Samoa for Tokelau with 25 people aboard — and never arrived. Five weeks later she was found drifting, half sunk and completely empty. The lifeboats were gone. Four tons of cargo were gone. Her radio was tuned to the distress channel. No trace of the 25 was ever found. Which side are you on?

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Sodder Children — Five Children Vanished From a Burning House
episodes.description: On Christmas Eve 1945, the Sodder house in Fayetteville, West Virginia burned to the ground — and five children vanished with it. No bones. No trace. The phone line was cut, the ladder was gone, and the trucks wouldn't start. Twenty-three years later, a photograph arrived that the family believed showed Louis, all grown up. Which side are you on?

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Lost Village of Anjikuni — An Entire Village Vanished Overnight
episodes.description: November 1930: a trapper reaches a frozen lake in northern Canada and finds an entire village gone — thirty people, dinner still on the table, no tracks leading away. The story spread around the world. But the Mounties investigated and found nothing. So was it a real vanishing — or the greatest ghost story ever printed? Which side are you on?

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Tunguska Blast — The Explosion With No Crater
episodes.description: June 30th, 1908: a fireball explodes over Siberia and flattens 2,150 square kilometres of forest — trees knocked down like matchsticks, all pointing away from one empty point in the sky. Nineteen years later, scientists finally reach the site. And there is nothing. No crater. No meteorite. Just a swamp where the sky exploded. So what was it? Which side are you on?

episodes.title: The Wow! Signal: The Isdal Woman — Eight Names, None of Them Hers
episodes.description: November 29th, 1970: hikers find a woman's body in a valley near Bergen, Norway. Every label is cut out of her clothes. Her fingerprints are gone. At the station, police find two suitcases — wigs, glasses she didn't need, money from five countries, and a little notebook full of code. She used at least eight fake identities. The police called it suicide. But who cuts the labels out of their own clothes? So who was she? Which side are you on?
